- Finding (AC3): the new rule accepts b = Q, n = P, h = P. Q enters rc_ok whenever rc_sha == Q (line 1093-1096 path), and P is always in rc_ok, so rc_named == P passes at 1160 and 1502. The old rule rejects this (b != P). AC3's rule (n in S) accepts it, but AC3's bound paragraph says "the run record must name Q". The contract is internally inconsistent; the code follows the rule. The state is still inside base = Q, head = P, but it is wider than the bound text states.
- AC3's bound sentence ("every accepted state is accepted with P emptied") is trivially true, since with P empty everything passes. It does not describe the widening against the base rule at P.
- Q == P: rc_ok = {P}, same as base. Inert with Q empty: HEX.fullmatch('') fails, rc_ok = {P}, condition equals the old one. Non-hex Q (uppercase, 'none', short, long) is never added. Branch run: same rule, no run-kind input. But P and Q come from the head's own workflow (188, 915, 1257), so a branch can declare both; only review guards them, as AC3 concedes.

(iii) Test:
- Finding: test_the_landing_passes (test lines 167-168) asserts the same call twice. The "task-branch" case is not a separate row, since the model has no run-kind input.
- test_the_table_tells_a_wrong_rule (217-223) and wrong_rule test the test's own model, not the workflow, so they cannot detect workflow drift.
- The truth table covers every AC5 row (167-215), but has no row for b = Q, n = P, h = P (see ii).
- Every new line is pinned once per step (NEW_LINES, 116-123) and the anchor order is pinned (125-134). Gaps: removal of the old message lines (`is not the pinned version %s` and `rc_sha, rc_named, PINNED_RC))`) is not pinned, only the old condition (136-140).
